facts.text: Pommes puree, the French potato puree, is smoother and denser than an everyday mash: the cooked potatoes are pressed through a ricer or food mill, or traditionally passed through a fine sieve called a tamis, and a large share of butter and cream is worked in; overworking makes potatoes gluey.

unsourced: How every web page was read: through search result summaries only (WebFetch is refused on this network). Each source says what its summary supported. A refuter with page access should open the pages behind any line that goes on a card.
Which herbs, the method, the butter and cream, and whether it is the same purée as the beef tenderloin plate: not printed, asked of the chef.
